title: Spinosaurus roar (sound design from real animal recordings)
author: DigiZoo sound design from recordings by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service; schots; National Park Service
changes: Movie-style dinosaur call: no recordings of dinosaurs exist, so it was designed from real animal recordings (American alligator bellows and a tiger snarl, pitched down and layered). Sound design from 3 real recordings: "Alligatorbellow1" 8.00–10.40 s, slowed to 0.85× speed (pitched down 15%); "439280 schots angry-tiger" 26.05–28.20 s, slowed to 0.75× speed (pitched down 25%), placed at 0.10 s; "Alligator (NPS Sound Gallery)" 3.60–5.00 s, slowed to 0.8× speed (pitched down 20%), placed at 0.60 s; then mixed to mono, gentle 12 dB/oct high-pass at 28 Hz, low-passed at 9000 Hz, added reverb, silence trimmed, loudness-normalised (≈ −18 dBFS RMS, peak ≤ −1 dBFS), 10 ms fade-in / 120 ms fade-out, encoded as 96 kbps mono MP3.
